cues.text: Hi, Howard. Haven't seen you for a while.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Hi Joanne. Yeah, they are keeping us really busy on the postgraduate program, but how are you? You'll be starting your dissertation soon, aren't you?
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Yeah, tutorials start next week. I've got Dr. Peterson. You'll remember still from last year, of course.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: It's not something you forget easily. But seriously, although I didn't expect to enjoy writing my dissertation, and in fact, I didn't really find it much fun, I wouldn't miss the experience.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: I found it really improved my understanding of the whole degree program, you know, from the first year on.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: So what are you doing yours on?
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Glaciated landscapes. Although I haven't decided exactly what aspect yet.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: I did mine on climate systems, so I can't help you much, I'm afraid. But you'll be fine once you start your tutorials. Dr. Peterson will help you focus.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: I know, and he'll set me deadlines for the different stages, which is what I need. My concern is that I've got tons of material on the topic, and I won't be able to stick to the word limit, you know?
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: I remember I had different concerns when I was doing my dissertation.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Last year?
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Yeah, before my first trial, I did a lot of fairly general reading because I haven't fixed on my topic at that stage. I actually enjoyed that quite a lot, and you know, it improved my reading speed.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: I had gotten through a lot of material, but I was frightened I wouldn't remember it all, so I got into the habit of making very detailed notes.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: So, did you find your tutor helpful in getting you started?
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Yeah, we certainly had some interesting discussions. But it's funny I saw a brilliant program about climate change, and it was that that fired me up. It was talking about some recent research which seemed to contradict some of the articles I've been reading.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: So you see your tutorials start next week
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Yeah.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Well, the first month was crucial. You've got to meet your tutor and decide your focus, but don't become too dependent on him. You know you don't see him every week, only when you want to check something
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Once you got the focus, you've got to get reading. It's helpful to look through the bibliographies for all the course modules relating to your topic and get hold of any books you think you'll need.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: I haven't got much money.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: I mean get the books from the library, far better.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: And I suppose I should prepare a detailed outline of the chapters.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Yeah, absolutely. But don't feel you have to follow it slavishly. It's meant to be flexible.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Okay. Now I'm someone who likes to get writing quickly. I can't just sit and read for a month.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Not like me then. But if that's what suits you, you know, your natural approach, then you want to start immediately and write the first chapter.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Now, Joanne. About the library, it's not worthwhile getting on good terms with the staff; they aren't always helpful with undergraduates.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: I suppose they focus on post-grads more.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Maybe. But show them you are serious about wanting to do good work.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: And what if I can't find what I need?
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Well, there're inter-library loans.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Borrowing books from the libraries. But I've heard it isn't all that reliable.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Hmm, you're right, but you probably won't need it anyway, be positive! The library is likely to have most things you need, and during the dissertation writing period, you can take out 15 instead of the usual 10 books.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Should I look at previous years' dissertations?
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: You can do.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: But I don't know which are the good ones.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: The library only keeps the best, and the staff can advise you.
cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: No.

cues.speaker: Howard

cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.speaker: Howard

cues.text: Gosh yeah, but I suppose I can get a lot of support from a couple of people who are thinking of doing the same topic as me.
cues.speaker: Joanne

cues.text: Take care, collaboration can become dependency! I think you'd better see how it works out, what the people are like.

cues.speaker: Joanne
